title: Metropolis posts ₹496.8 crore revenue in Q2 FY27, profit jumps 42.7%
summary: Patient volume grew 10 per cent YoY to 4.1 million, while test volume increased 11 per cent to 8.7 million, reflecting sustained demand and a continued shift towards organised diagnostic providers, the company said.

New Delhi: Metropolis Healthcare reported a 15.8 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in revenue from operations to Rs 496.8 crore in Q2 FY27. Reported EBITDA increased 23.9 per cent YoY to Rs 134.9 crore, while profit after tax (PAT) rose 42.7 per cent to Rs 75.5 crore in the quarter ended September 2026.Patient volume grew 10 per cent YoY to 4.1 million, while test volume increased 11 per cent to 8.7 million, reflecting sustained demand and a continued shift towards organised diagnostic providers, the company said.

The business-to-consumer (B2C) segment recorded 17 per cent YoY revenue growth to Rs 289 crore, while business-to-business (B2B) revenue increased 15 per cent to Rs 208 crore.

Advt

TruHealth revenue grew 20 per cent YoY to Rs 86 crore, driven by premiumisation and increased adoption of preventive care. Specialty revenue also rose 20 per cent to Rs 198 crore, led by advanced genomic testing and growth in cancer testing.

Revenue per patient (RPP) increased 6 per cent YoY to Rs 1,221, despite the absence of any price increase benefit. Revenue per test (RPT) improved 5 per cent to Rs 572, supported by a richer test mix and improved realisations.Metropolis said Tier III cities remained its fastest-growing markets, with revenue rising around 20 per cent YoY. The company now has a presence across approximately 750 towns through 5,119 service points.

For the six months ended September 2026, Metropolis reported a 16.2 per cent YoY increase in revenue to Rs 947 crore, while PAT rose 34.9 per cent to Rs 132.4 crore.Ameera Shah, Promoter and Executive Chairperson, Metropolis Healthcare Limited, said, “As diagnostics becomes central to preventive and precision healthcare, we are building Metropolis into a stronger, differentiated and future-ready platform. We will deepen our science and genomics expertise, use technology to transform the patient experience, and pursue strategic acquisitions that sharpen our competitive edge. From a 1,000-gene oncology panel to a blood-based Alzheimer’s test, our newest offerings bring earlier answers to complex clinical questions. Under Metropolis 3.0, our priority is not simply to expand our footprint, but to create the capabilities that will define the next phase of Indian diagnostics.”
